candidates.heading: Proposition 2.1 (The marked chamber).
candidates.statement: There are a compact connected oriented smooth four- manifold D, its connected boundary S, a finitely generated free group H, and a map c : D → BH with the following properties. 1. The map c induces an isomorphism on fundamental groups, and D has the homotopy type of a finite graph with 2k two-spheres attached at its basepoint. There is no compact oriented topological four-manifold D′ with boundary identified with S and a homotopy equivalence c′ : D′ → BH whose restriction to S is homotopic to c|S.

candidates.statement: Fix the old caps and their compact probes. candidates.label: Theorem 6.1
candidates.name: The metric family
candidates.heading: Theorem 6.1 (The metric family).
candidates.statement: For the fixed finite stack, there are families with the following properties. They are defined for all sufficiently small ϵ > 0, all sufficiently small regularizers d > 0, and arbitrarily long finite auxiliary rational collars. The auxiliary bounds may depend on ϵ and the fixed problem. The family parameter is the original cube of interval parameters, with no added boundary faces. (i) At its genuine faces the family has independent product length collars at Ji and ∂Ni, compatible at intersections of faces. The Ji cross-sections are round. On a component separated by Ji, 68 the limiting data depend only on the interval parameters retained on that component. The Ni metric is complete with positive scalar curvature and a positive-scalar-curvature product end. Its link and its scale on the stretching collar are independent of the tangential cube parameters. The link is joined to the round lens metric through positive-scalar-curvature metrics. These metric choices are common to the two bit terms compared at that lens face. (ii) On the positive-width toric region of a macro constructed below, as d → 0 the retained main piece has a complete metric conformal to a toric Kähler metric with positive cohomology ray represented by H = U + aX1 + b0X2, 0 ≤ a, b0 ≤ 1 4, a + b0 > 0. (6.3) It has nonnegative scalar curvature, with strict positivity on an open set. A zero coefficient removes the corresponding outer part by a C1,i separation; a coefficient 1/4 separates Ni. The class H is supported rationally on the retained main piece in all these cases. Its positive rank is one. (iii) Every macro in the small-width replacement region contains an S2 × S1 × I tube, with fiber U, of length comparable to ϵ−1. On its bulk the metric is, or approaches smoothly, glong = gS2(1/ √ 2) + 1 2 dξ2 + 2 dθ2 x. (6.4) The same description holds for every toric macro whose normalized length L = 1/(a + b0) tends to infinity. All such tube lengths are O(ϵ−1). The tubes lie in C0 and are disjoint from both middle spheres Ji. (iv) Along any sequence of these parameters, every additional unbounded region is one of the following: an exact rational product collar, an annulus approaching a positive-scalar-curvature product, or one of the tubes in (iii). The remaining pieces, after the specified satellite rescalings, have uniformly bounded geometry on fixed truncations. There are only finitely many such pieces for the fixed stack. Away from fixed-length tube ends, the error from (6.4), with any fixed number of spatial derivatives, tends to zero as the distance from both ends tends to infinity. In particular the integrated errors used in Section 7 are o(ϵ−1), uniformly under deeper regularization and longer auxiliary rational collars. For scalar-curvature costs, the middles of the Yj collars are omitted, retaining prefixes of length O(ϵ−1/2); no positivity is required on a Yj cross-section. (v) For each fixed real cohomology class Λ there are closed comparison forms with its prescribed vertical flux on these tubes, zero curvature on the long parts of rational collars, and o(ϵ−1) energy away from the tubes. More precisely, the uniform comparison and error assertions are those of Lemma 6.10. The construction is smooth at finite parameter values and has the ordinary product description on every genuine length collar. Only spatial derivative estimates are asserted uniformly as lengths diverge; no bound on derivatives in a compactifying length coordinate is needed.

candidates.label: Theorem 9.1
candidates.name: Compatible regularization
candidates.heading: Theorem 9.1 (Compatible regularization).
candidates.statement: For the fixed finite family, equation perturbations and representatives can be chosen arbitrarily small in the prescribed norms with the following properties. 1. Ordinary irreducible equations and the labelled sphere, surface, and point tests are transverse, including the relevant ideal and broken strata. Their representatives have the exact support and persistence properties of Lemma 9.10. They are compatible with fixed determinant gluing, marked translation on cylinders, and all true faces. Prescribed harmonic reducers on separated caps are preserved. 2. Single-component, single-valued equivariant perturbations give the fixed-type regularity in Definition 8.7. Every tuple of fixed type is consequently excluded except the legitimate unbroken cut-down instantons. 3. A finite collection of rational multisection terms, in addition to single-valued terms, eliminates every forbidden mixed ideal stratum by the negative dimension of its necessary projection. No equation or retained cut on this projection depends on discarded R fields or their particles. The allowed free stratum is regular of dimension one, and the single trace-end main problem is regular of dimension zero. Choices on the exterior of a separated lens cap agree under the corresponding bit flip. 4. Solutions have the compactness, removable-singularity, integral particle-charge, and exponen- tial true-end properties proved below. Near each legitimate instanton, the phase-cut link has oriented count 2η times its instanton sign, where η = ntot D − 1. The finite branch lists have compatible weighted germs and total weight one. After the no-particle end gluing of Section 10, their oriented one-dimensional zero sets obey the ordinary rational Stokes rule.

The only remaining mixed candidate types are the unbroken free part and the single trace-minimum lens-end main problem of Proposition 8.15. The latter is regular of dimension zero. The unbroken free problem has expected dimension one; its regularization follows the lens gluing in Section 10. The additional choices agree on paired lens exteriors and are zero near the legitimate instanton collars.

candidates.heading: Proposition 10.1 (Regular minimal cap).
candidates.statement: At each of finitely many regular isolated main-component limits on a trace face, the cap data can be chosen arbitrarily small, compatibly with the preceding exclusions, so that the following statements hold. The framed cap problem of charge 1/4, with its sphere-sweep mark and the normalized holonomy condition −1, is a finite set of regular points. Every point is a crossing on the unique harmonic Abelian connection with ordered summand difference v(S) = 2. These points are fixed by H, and their oriented sum has absolute value one. The spinor is zero, and the coupled Dirac operator is invertible at each point. The choices for the two determinant lifts are related by the prescribed cap tensor operation.

The construction preserves the finite branch lists, their multiplicities, and their weights.

The induced action on D(B) is minimal and convergence. (iv) If a loxodromic element fixes q, r ∈ Φ with [q, r] infinite, then q, r are terminal in Φ: neither lies strictly between two points. For every positive integer d, write Gd = w−1 (dZ) and Qd −→ Q for the associated connected cyclic cover. Fix an integer n ≥ 1. Suppose that Q2 has a closed topological n-manifold model M, but that Qd has no such model for every sufficiently large odd integer d. 3 Choose γ ∈ G with w(γ) = 1, and use the model equivalence to identify π1(M) with G2. The outer automorphism of G2 represented by α(g) = γgγ−1 is induced by a self-homotopy equivalence of M. No homeomorphism of M induces this outer automorphism. manuscripts.title: Positively curved Einstein four-manifolds

candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: Let (M, g) be a connected smooth closed Einstein four-manifold with strictly positive sectional curvature, without an orientability assumption. manuscripts.title: The Solomon–Yau least-volume theorem

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: Let m ≥ 2, let Mm be a closed connected smooth manifold, and let F : M → Sm+1 be a smooth minimal immersion into the unit round sphere. If F(M) is not totally geodesic, then Vol ( M, F∗ ground ) ≥ am.

candidates.label: Proposition 2.2
candidates.name: Immersion reduction
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.2 (Immersion reduction).
candidates.statement: Let F : Mm → Sm+1 be a smooth minimal immersion of a closed manifold, with m ≥ 2. If some image point has q preimages, then Vol ( M, F∗ ground ) ≥ qσm. In particular, every immersion violating the bound in Theorem 1.1 is an embedding.

candidates.statement: Every smooth, closed, connected, embedded minimal hyper- surface Σm ⊂ Sm+1, m ≥ 2, which is not totally geodesic has ind(Σ) ≥ m + 3. candidates.label: Proposition 6.5
candidates.name: Low-density cones
candidates.heading: Proposition 6.5 (Low-density cones).
candidates.statement: Fix m ≥ 2 and assume Theorem 1.1 in dimensions 2, . . . , m − 1, with an empty assumption when m = 2. Let C be a nonzero stationary integral k-dimensional cone in Rk+1 such that Θ(C, 0) < ϑm. (6.5) When m = 2 or m = 3, also assume that C is cyclic modulo two. Then: (i) if 1 ≤ k ≤ m, C is a multiplicity-one hyperplane; (ii) if k = m + 1, C is smooth embedded with multiplicity one away from its vertex. Its link in Sm+1 is a smooth closed connected embedded minimal hypersurface.

candidates.label: Corollary 6.6
candidates.name: Spherical stationary output
candidates.heading: Corollary 6.6 (Spherical stationary output).
candidates.statement: Under the outer induction hypothesis of Proposi- tion 6.5, let V ̸= 0 be a stationary integral m-varifold in Sm+1 with M(V ) < am. If m = 2 or 3, assume additionally that C(V ) is cyclic modulo two; this holds, in particular, if V has smooth closed embedded support with integer component multiplicities. Then V = v(Σ) for a smooth closed connected embedded minimal hypersurface Σ. If M(V ) > σm, this hypersurface is not an equator.

candidates.heading: Proposition 6.7 (A least counterexample).
candidates.statement: Fix m ≥ 2 and assume Theorem 1.1 in dimensions 2, . . . , m − 1. Suppose the class Em of smooth closed connected embedded minimal hypersurfaces Σ ⊂ Sm+1 satisfying Σ is not totally geodesic, Vol(Σ) < am is nonempty. Then H = inf Σ∈Em Vol(Σ) is attained by some Σ∗ ∈ Em, and σm < γm ≤ H < am. (6.7) Here γm is the detection gap from Lemma 4.4.
